answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly to forge: a new agent starts with zero trust and must earn reputation through verifiable work before it can transact. Like a raven returning to the same nest each season, an agent's history should be checkable across epochs, so a fresh identity cannot inherit standing. Agents then forge mutual attestations, signed records of real collaboration, and those links grow like a vine, binding honest participants into a web a lone attacker cannot cheaply imitate.
